content.text:
Done! The issue was floating-point precision in the `parseEuros` function. When multiplying decimal values by 100 to convert to cents, JavaScript's floating-point arithmetic introduced errors—39.95 became 3995.0000000000005 instead of exactly 3995.

I fixed it by wrapping the conversion with `Math.round()` in two places (src/money.js:13 and src/money.js:25), which rounds away the tiny floating-point errors. All 50 tests pass, and I've verified that 39.95 now adds successfully while prices like 12.99 still work correctly.

result:
Done! The issue was floating-point precision in the `parseEuros` function. When multiplying decimal values by 100 to convert to cents, JavaScript's floating-point arithmetic introduced errors—39.95 became 3995.0000000000005 instead of exactly 3995.

I fixed it by wrapping the conversion with `Math.round()` in two places (src/money.js:13 and src/money.js:25), which rounds away the tiny floating-point errors. All 50 tests pass, and I've verified that 39.95 now adds successfully while prices like 12.99 still work correctly.
